note: Inputs that would look like a real credential are recipes: `template` with {t} replaced by each part`s prefix + rnd(len, abc), where rnd(n, abc) = Array.from({length:n}, (_, i) => abc[(i*7+3) % abc.length]).join("") and abc defaults to [a-zA-Z0-9]. The conformance runner materialises them; no credential-shaped literal is stored. `deep` cases are JSON values: `in` run through the structured walk (redactDeep) gives `out`, and `out` gives itself. An adversarial case with `under` is walked as the one string under that key. The cases that are read one character at a time have a wider budget: instrumented for coverage they run several times slower, and a reader that stopped being linear would take far longer than that.
